In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the stress distribution in the cortical bone surrounding the dental implants in the edentulous patient after midline maxillogectomy was affected by the design of the implant retained obturator prosthesis, type of the attachments, the location of the loading and the magnitude of the applied load.
ball & socket attachments exhibited the lowest stress values, then the magnet, and finally the bar & clips attachments.
the bar & clips attachment design showed the highest stress value in all load conditions, and the ball & socket design showed the lowest stresses in all load conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ball & socket model exhibited the best stress distribution followed by the magnet model then the bar & clip models.

the ball & socket model exhibited the lowest stress values under unilateral oblique load that was applied on the defect site, while the bar & clips model exhibited the highest stress values in the same situation.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the implant retained obturator with the ball & socket attachment is a good choice in terms of stress distribution in the bone around dental implant in cases of mid-line maxillectomy.
the implant supported obturators with ball and socket attachments are the most suitable for rehabilitation of midline defects, followed by magnet attachments, then the bar & clip attachment.
